standard_title: OIML R 76-1:2006 (E) Non-automatic weighing instruments - Part 1

national_adoption.clause: Seventh Schedule, Heading A [See Rule 13], Part II, para 3(3) / Table 17
deviations: Ordinary accuracy class symbol is 'IV' in India, 'IIII' in OIML. Values are unchanged.
Multi-interval Maxi/ei+1 thresholds appear as Table 18 in the Indian schedule (identical to OIML Table 4).

transcription_note: Band values and comparison operators taken from the OIML R 76-1:2006 PDF text layer, NOT from the Indian Kanoon text rendering of the Seventh Schedule, whose operators are corrupted (it renders '5000 < m' as '5000 <= m', producing overlapping bands).

classes.name: Special accuracy
notes: e < 1 mg is not normally feasible to test and verify, due to the uncertainty of the test loads (Table 3 footnote *).
For an instrument of class I with d < 0.1 mg, n may be less than 50 000 (3.4.4).

min_capacity_rules.grading_instruments_note: Min is reduced to 5 e for grading instruments, i.e. instruments that determine a transport tariff or toll (e.g. postal scales, instruments weighing waste material). Table 3, following text.
min_capacity_rules.auxiliary_indicating_device_note: Where the instrument has an auxiliary indicating device, the multiplier in the Min column applies to the actual scale interval d instead of e (3.4.3).

multi_interval.rule: With the exception of the last partial weighing range, Maxi / e(i+1) shall be >= the threshold for the class.

scale_interval_form.rule: e shall be of the form 1 x 10^k, 2 x 10^k or 5 x 10^k, k being a positive or negative whole number or zero.

multiple_range_notes: On multiple range instruments the verification scale intervals are e1 < e2 < ... < er; Min, n and Max are subscripted accordingly.
On multiple range instruments, each range is treated as if it were an instrument with one range.
For special applications clearly marked on the instrument, ranges may be in classes I and II, or II and III; the instrument as a whole shall comply with the more severe requirements of 3.9.
